issues: Wrong figure. The correction states that the program called the page '13,504 times' for 'a virtual DM 134,634.88'. Only heise gives that figure. The Bundespost's own final statement to Steffen Wernéry, dated 1 April 1985 (scan at wauland.de/media/btx-hack/1985-04-01_Btx-Abrechnung.pdf, read visually), lists 'Hamburger Sparkasse ... 13.11.-16.12.84 ... 134.694,70' among unpaid provider fees. That is 13,510 × DM 9.97. The Wau Holland Stiftung page gives the same numbers ('overnight they obtained 134.694,70 DM, which represents 13510 page views', --check FOUND), and so does German Wikipedia (Btx-Hack). The correction now uses the Bundespost figure and mentions heise's figure as an alternative.

Verified. The CCC press release 'Kennwort: Bankraub' of 19 November 1984 (scan at wauland.de/media/btx-hack/1984-11-19_PM-CCC.pdf, read visually; it has no text layer, so --check cannot run) says the demonstration took place on 19.11.1984 on the premises of the Hamburg data protection commissioner. It also says the CCC 'erhebt jedoch keinen Anspruch auf das Geld' and ends with 'ganz abschalten oder Verbot aller Finanztransaktionen'. This supports 'went public at once' and the call for a ban. The Wauland page also says 'On Monday, November 19th, 1984, the BTX hack was made public' (--check FOUND). Both points are now stated explicitly.

Checked OK. sources[0]: heise online (Detlef Borchers), 2024-11-18. Both the quote and the note's '9.97 marks, which theoretically went to the CCC' --check FOUND. heise also supports the October 1984 warning ('had already written to German data protection authorities and the German Federal Post Office in October 1984') and the 'ban on financial transactions'. Its DM 134,634.88 / 13,504 total conflicts with the Bundespost statement; this is flagged in the source note.

Checked OK. sources[1]: Wau Holland Stiftung '30th anniversary' page; the quote ('"bank theft" of 135.000 DM') --check FOUND. The page's dated entries run to November 2014, so the date 2014-11 is fine.

fieldFixes.correction: The 'bank robbery' was a demonstration. On the night of 16–17 November 1984, using the Hamburger Sparkasse's Btx login, a small program called up a CCC page priced at DM 9.97 about 13,500 times. That ran up a virtual DM 134,694.70 (the figure on the Bundespost's own 1985 statement; heise gives DM 134,634.88) that 'theoretically went to the CCC'. The club had warned the Bundespost and data-protection officials in October 1984. On Monday 19 November it demonstrated the hack at the Hamburg data-protection commissioner's office, told the press, made no claim to the money and called for a ban on financial transactions on Btx.

sourceFixes.note: Re-fetched 2026-09-23; quote --check FOUND. heise's 13,504 × DM 9.97 = DM 134,634.88 differs from the Bundespost's 1985 statement (DM 134,694.70 = 13,510 × 9.97), which the Wau Holland Stiftung and German Wikipedia follow.
